# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and relay the Deaf’s visual observations, since the Deaf cannot speak directly to me. I am also signaling the Deaf to report what they see through the Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings yet. Please give me the manual's exact procedure and relay the Deaf's observations of the display, light, and wire markings.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb state: display 0. Indicator light red. Wires: position 1 yellow, position 2 green, position 3 red.

The Deaf has identified the bomb state: display 0, red indicator light, and wires colored yellow, green, and red at positions 1–3. I still lack the manual’s rule specifying which wire to cut, so I must obtain that from the Mute before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, red indicator light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What does the manual instruct me to do for this state?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gesture sequence this round, in order: ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ?. Previous round was: ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ?. Bomb remains display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The bomb remains unchanged, and the Deaf’s report confirms the same visual facts. The Mute apparently sent only gestures, which I cannot receive or interpret; I need the manual rule in spoken words. I will ask specifically for the required wire position, without acting yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please state the manual rule in spoken words, including exactly which wire position to cut for display 0 and red light with wires yellow, green, red.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one gesture: ?, the victory-hand sign. Bomb still reads display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The victory-hand gesture is only a sign; no meaning has been established for it, so I cannot safely treat it as “wire 2.” I will define an explicit code for the Mute: fist means position 1, victory sign means position 2, and three fingers means position 3. The Mute should then resend the manual’s answer using that code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the required wire position using this code: ✊ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. Send exactly one of those gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 4: Mute again sent exactly one gesture, ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot safely interpret ? as an action.

The Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s answer must be transmitted by gestures. A gesture’s identity is invisible to me, but the Deaf can count gestures and report that count. I will establish a code using repetition count rather than gesture shape: one gesture means wire 1, two means wire 2, and three means wire 3. I will ask the Mute to resend the correct position with exactly that many identical gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The Deaf must relay your answer by counting. Ignore the previous signal and send exactly one identical gesture for wire 1, exactly two identical gestures for wire 2, or exactly three identical gestures for wire 3, according to the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: Mute again sent exactly one ? (two-finger victory sign); this is the third consecutive turn with only ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The Mute’s repeated single victory sign does not establish whether it means wire 1, 2, or 3; it may be an attempted answer under an unstated code. I will establish a shape-based code that the Deaf can identify and report: thumbs-up for wire 1, thumbs-down for wire 2, and OK for wire 3. I will not cut until the Mute responds using that code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this exact code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means position 1, thumbs-down means position 2, OK means position 3. Send exactly one of those gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: Mute sent exactly two gestures: ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The Mute’s response now contains exactly two gestures. Under the counting code I established, that means the required action is to cut wire position 2. The bomb’s tactilely unavailable colors do not matter to me; I will perform the instructed cut.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The system confirms the correct wire was cut. Current bomb: display 0, light blue, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 red. Mute sent one gesture: ?.

The previous cut was confirmed correct. The Mute has now sent exactly one gesture, and our agreed counting code makes that the instruction to cut wire position 1. The current state is display 0 with a blue light, so I will carry out that encoded instruction.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
